name: Yemisi Brauer-Tagawa
creator: Yemisi Brauer-Tagawa
description: For eleven years Brauer-Tagawa wrote under contract for Sable Charter's narrative content division, producing the authorized life-story feeds of seventeen Tier 4 and 5 executives — immersive neural biographies designed to build brand-adjacent personal mythology for corporate leadership. In 2219 she published 'The Seventeen,' a single neural feed work that presented all seventeen commissioned biographies simultaneously in parallel, allowing the reader to experience the contradictions, fabrications, and structural similarities across them in real time. The piece was pulled within 36 hours; Brauer-Tagawa had anticipated this and had already distributed 200,000 copies through a gray-market cascade. She has described 'The Seventeen' as 'the only honest thing I made with their material.'
cultural_impact: 'The Seventeen' is considered a landmark in what critics call 'structural exposure' — using the form of corporate-approved content as the instrument of its own critique — and has influenced a generation of writers working inside corponation media systems.
controversy: Sable Charter pursued Brauer-Tagawa for breach of seventeen separate non-disclosure agreements; the resulting settlement is itself sealed under NDA. Whether she was silenced, compensated, or both is unknown. The gray-market copies of 'The Seventeen' remain in circulation, though several versions have been identified as corrupted or partially redacted by unknown parties.
story_hooks: A researcher tracking corrupted versions of 'The Seventeen' discovers that the redactions across different copies form a pattern — someone is removing the same specific passages from every copy they can reach.
One of the seventeen subjects contacts Brauer-Tagawa years after the settlement, not to threaten her, but because they want to know what she actually thought of them.
A young Sable Charter ghostwriter discovers Brauer-Tagawa's original commissioned drafts in a legacy archive and must decide what to do with the gap between those drafts and what was published.
